analysis:
The PR only modifies docs/architecture/inference.md. The changed ranges (head 1087-1090, 1100-1146, 2028-2041) are the scheduler prefill-geometry table, which sits outside the two supplied base_text units (base lines 1638-2205). The patch excerpt is truncated, so I could not see the full changes. What I could see is the new description of default prefill chunk and step sizes: 2048/4096 for GPT-OSS, dense Qwen3.5/3.8 and Gemma 4, and 512/2048 elsewhere. It also describes the solo-prefill stripe and a bidirectional media prefill chunk ceiling of 512. These are documentation of scheduler tuning knobs. The excerpt shows no change to authorization, attestation, encryption, key handling, prefix-cache TTL, the SSD tier, cacheSalt scoping or the coordinator-provider trust boundary. Its only possible security relevance is availability and memory pressure (T-010 and T-029 style concerns): wider prefill chunks could raise transient memory use. The docs say that memory admission, KV budgets and process ledgers remain mandatory, and nothing in the visible text weakens them.

The supplied base text (MiMo native candidate, Flint, coordinator-serving channels, invariants) is unchanged context. It was read against T-041 and TB-007, and no regression is introduced. The prefix-cache statements in it (SSD reuse defaults, media being noncacheable, encrypted-store ownership) are consistent with the T-041 mitigations.

Remaining uncertainty: the patch for head lines 1100-1146 and 2028-2041 is not visible. A later pass should confirm that those hunks do not change any documented security invariant. The prefillGeometry claims are also not verified against source here, since this is a docs-only change and the code is not supplied.
